+def _rank_supports(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[frozenset, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-coordinate supports in the rank hypergraph."""
+    coordinates = prime_divisors(n)
+    supports = []
+    for prime, exponent in sorted(
+        (int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(m).items()
+    ):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime**exponent, n)
+        supports.append(
+            frozenset(i for i, ell in enumerate(coordinates) if rank % ell == 0)
+        )
+    return tuple(supports)
+
+
+def _supports_are_connected(supports: Sequence[frozenset], k: int) -> bool:
+    if k == 1:
+        return True
+    adjacency = [set() for _ in range(k)]
+    for support in supports:
+        for vertex in support:
+            adjacency[vertex].update(support - {vertex})
+    reached = {0}
+    frontier = [0]
+    while frontier:
+        vertex = frontier.pop()
+        for neighbor in adjacency[vertex] - reached:
+            reached.add(neighbor)
+            frontier.append(neighbor)
+    return len(reached) == k
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def support_spectra(n: int) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    """Compute the total and connected omega-spectra of M_n exactly."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    total = set()
+    connected = set()
+    for m in upper_fiber_threshold(n).minimal_generators:
+        size = omega(m)
+        total.add(size)
+        if _supports_are_connected(_rank_supports(m, n), k):
+            connected.add(size)
+    return tuple(sorted(total)), tuple(sorted(connected))
+
+
+def expected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted total support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    has_extremal_slice = not (2 in factors and all(e == 1 for e in factors.values()))
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+def expected_connected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted connected support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    if k == 1:
+        return (1,)
+    squarefree = all(e == 1 for e in factors.values())
+    rank_six_orientation_obstruction = (
+        factors.get(2) == 2
+        and factors.get(3) == 1
+        and all(e == 1 for p, e in factors.items() if p not in (2, 3))
+    )
+    has_connected_extremal_slice = (
+        not squarefree and not rank_six_orientation_obstruction
+    )
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_connected_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def extremal_support_product_count(n: int) -> int:
+    """Count the product of the k singleton diagonal atomic families."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("the extremal slice is stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    counts = [0] * k
+    for prime, top_exponent in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        for exponent in range(1, top_exponent + 1):
+            theta = prime**exponent
+            if alpha_for_fn_divisor(theta, n) == alpha_for_fn_divisor(
+                prime ** (exponent - 1), n
+            ):
+                continue
+            essential, full = _support_pairs(theta, n)[0]
+            if essential == full and len(full) == 1:
+                counts[next(iter(full))] += 1
+    return math.prod(counts)
+

+\begin{theorem}[Exact support spectra and the extremal slice]
+\label{thm:exact-support-spectra}
+Let $n\ge3$, write
+\[
+ n=\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\ell^{a_\ell},
+ \qquad k=\omega(n),
+\]
+and put
+\[
+ \Sigma(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n\},\qquad
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n^{\rm conn}\}.
+\]
+For each $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$, define the singleton diagonal atomic family
+\[
+ \mathcal A_\ell(n):=
+ \mathcal A_{\{\ell\},\{\ell\}}(n).
+\]
+Then multiplication gives a bijection
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection}
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\mathcal A_\ell(n)
+ \longrightarrow
+ \{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\},
+ \qquad (\theta_\ell)_\ell\longmapsto
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\theta_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+In particular,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-count}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\}
+ =\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\#\mathcal A_\ell(n).
+\end{equation}
+The complete support spectrum is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},&n\text{ is even and squarefree},\\
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+For the connected spectrum, $\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=\{1\}$ when $k=1$.
+If $k\ge2$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},
+   &\begin{array}{l}
+     n\text{ is squarefree, or }n=12s\text{ with }s\text{ squarefree}\
+     \text{and }\gcd(s,6)=1,
+    \end{array}\\[2mm]
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first classify the extremal slice. Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ have
+$\omega(m)=k$, and let $\Theta(m)$ be its witness cover. For every
+$\theta\in\Theta(m)$, choose a private coordinate
+\[
+ \ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
+ \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta(m),\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta).
+\]
+The chosen coordinates are distinct, since a coordinate chosen for two atoms
+would lie in the full support of each and hence would not be private to either.
+There are $k$ atoms and $k$ coordinates, so $\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a
+bijection. If $q\ne\ell(\theta)$, then $q$ is private to another atom and
+therefore cannot lie in $T_n(\theta)$. Hence
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=E_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}.
+\]
+Thus the inverse of \eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection} sends $m$
+to its uniquely labelled atoms in the families $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$.
+
+Conversely, choose $\theta_\ell\in\mathcal A_\ell(n)$ for every
+$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$.
+These atoms are pairwise coprime. Indeed, if
+$\theta_\ell=p^e$ and $\theta_q=p^f$ had the same underlying prime, then
+$e\ne f$ because the same atom cannot lie in two differently labelled
+families. Say $e<f$. Then $p^e\mid p^{f-1}$ would give
+\[
+ d(\theta_\ell)\mid d^-(\theta_q).
+\]
+Since $\ell$ occurs to its full $n$-adic exponent in $d(\theta_\ell)$, it
+would also occur fully in $d(\theta_q)$, contrary to
+$T_n(\theta_q)=\{q\}$ and $q\ne\ell$. The singleton full supports cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and the singleton essential supports are private. Hence the
+chosen atoms form an $n$-witness cover. The witness-cover theorem proves that
+their product belongs to $\mathcal M_n$ and has $k$ distinct prime factors.
+Uniqueness follows from unique factorization. This proves the bijection and
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count}.
+
+We next decide when the factors on the right of
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count} are nonzero. If $\ell$ is odd, or
+if $\ell=2$ and $a_2\ge2$, then the exact-rank existence theorem supplies a
+prime of rank $\ell^{a_\ell}$; this is an element of
+$\mathcal A_\ell(n)$. Suppose now that $a_2=1$. If $n$ is squarefree and
+$\theta\in\mathcal A_2(n)$, then $d(\theta)\mid n$ cannot contain an odd
+coordinate: every such coordinate would occur fully and would belong to
+$T_n(\theta)$. Thus $d(\theta)=2$, which is impossible because $F_2=1$ and
+$\Atom(2)=\varnothing$. Therefore the extremal slice is empty when $n$ is
+even and squarefree.
+
+If instead $a_2=1$ and $q^2\mid n$ for some odd prime $q$, take an atom of
+rank $2q$. For $q=3$, the atom $4\in\Atom(6)$ has, relative to $n$,
+$E_n(4)=T_n(4)=\{2\}$. For $q\ge5$, the rank $2q$ is nonexceptional, so an
+exact-rank prime exists and again has essential and full support $\{2\}$,
+because the $q$-coordinate is sub-full in $n$. Thus
+$\mathcal A_2(n)\ne\varnothing$. All other diagonal families were already
+seen to be nonempty, proving that the support value $k$ occurs exactly in the
+second case of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+It remains to realize every smaller support size. Assume $k\ge2$ and
+$1\le r\le k-1$. Choose a partition $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P(n)$ into $r$
+nonempty blocks, with the additional condition that $\{2\}$ is not a block
+when $a_2=1$. Such a partition exists because $r<k$. For $C\in\Pi$, put
+$n_C=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{a_\ell}$ and choose
+$\theta_C\in\Atom(n_C)$. This is possible by exact-rank prime existence
+unless $n_C\in\{6,12\}$; in those two cases use respectively
+$4\in\Atom(6)$ and $16\in\Atom(12)$. The forbidden rank $2$ was excluded by
+the choice of $\Pi$. Strong divisibility makes the atoms belonging to
+disjoint blocks pairwise coprime. Their full supports are the blocks $C$, and
+each has a nonempty essential support because lowering it decreases its rank.
+They therefore form an $n$-witness cover. Its product has exactly $r$ prime
+factors, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+The same idea gives all connected support sizes below $k$. Choose a hub
+$h\in\mathcal P(n)$, taking $h=3$ whenever
+$\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ and $n_{\{2,3\}}\in\{6,12\}$, and partition
+$\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{h\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.
+Use one atom of exact rank $n_{\{h\}\cup P_i}$ for each $i$. The only
+exceptional support that can occur is $\{2,3\}$; use $4$ at rank $6$ or $16$
+at rank $12$. In both cases its essential support contains the private
+coordinate $2\in P_i$. Every nonexceptional atom is a prime atom and has any
+coordinate of the nonempty set $P_i$ as a private coordinate. The atoms are
+pairwise coprime: their ranks are distinct, and the exceptional atom has
+underlying prime $2$, whose rank $3$ is not one of the other multi-coordinate
+ranks. The resulting witness cover is connected because all its rank-support
+edges contain $h$. Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}
+ \{1,\ldots,k-1\}\subseteq\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)\qquad(k\ge2).
+\end{equation}
+
+We finally decide whether the endpoint $k$ can be connected. In an extremal
+witness cover, write $\theta_\ell$ for the atom with
+$T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}$ and let
+$S_\ell=\operatorname{supp}_n(d(\theta_\ell))$ be its positive-coordinate
+rank support. If $q\in S_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}$, then
+\[
+ 1\le\nu_q(d(\theta_\ell))<a_q,
+\]
+so necessarily $a_q\ge2$. If $n$ is squarefree, every $S_\ell$ is therefore
+the singleton $\{\ell\}$, and the rank-support hypergraph is disconnected
+when $k\ge2$.
+
+There is one further obstruction. Let $n=12s$ with $s$ squarefree and
+$\gcd(s,6)=1$. The only coordinate of exponent at least two is $2$. Hence an
+edge $S_3$ larger than $\{3\}$ would force $d(\theta_3)=6$. But
+$\Atom(6)=\{4\}$, and lowering $4$ gives rank $3$; relative to this $n$, the
+$3$-coordinate is not lost. Thus an atom of rank $6$ with
+$T_n(\theta_3)=\{3\}$ has empty essential support and cannot occur in a
+witness cover. Consequently $S_3=\{3\}$. Since $a_3=1$, the coordinate $3$
+cannot occur sub-fully in any other $S_\ell$, so it is isolated and the
+extremal generator is disconnected.
+
+Conversely, suppose that $n$ is nonsquarefree and is not of the preceding
+form. Choose a coordinate $h$ with $a_h\ge2$. If possible take $h\ne2$. For
+each $\ell\ne h$, choose an atom of rank
+\[
+ d_\ell=\ell^{a_\ell}h,
+\]
+and choose an exact-rank prime of rank $h^{a_h}$ for the $h$-atom. The ranks
+$d_\ell$ are nonexceptional except possibly when $h=3$ and $\ell=2$; use
+$4$ when $d_2=6$ and $16$ when $d_2=12$. These exceptional atoms have
+$E_n=T_n=\{2\}$ because the $3$-coordinate is sub-full. If the only possible
+hub is $h=2$, then either $3\nmid n$ or $a_2\ge3$. In the latter case, use
+$9\in\Atom(12)$ for the $3$-atom; relative to $n$ it has
+$E_n(9)=T_n(9)=\{3\}$. Use exact-rank primes of rank
+$\ell^{a_\ell}2$ for the remaining nonhub coordinates. In every case we have
+chosen one atom from each $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$, so the extremal-slice
+bijection makes their product a minimal generator. Its rank-support edges are
+$\{h\}$ and the pairs $\{h,\ell\}$, hence it is connected. Together with
+\eqref{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}, this proves
+\eqref{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound-sharp}
+For $n\ge3$, there exists $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with
+$\omega(m)=\omega(n)$ if and only if $n$ is not even and squarefree. In
+particular, equality occurs on every odd layer.
+\end{corollary}

+\begin{proof}
+This is the endpoint assertion in \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}

+## Deep Exploration Check: Exact Support Spectra
+
+Checked 2026-08-08. Fresh queries were sent to the arXiv Atom API, Crossref,
+Semantic Scholar, and zbMATH Open for Fibonacci ranks of apparition, minimal
+generators, minimal covers, connected hypergraphs, split graphs, primitive
+divisors, and strong divisibility sequences. Semantic Scholar's keyword-search
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 from the shared address, so the three nearest known
+papers were checked there by DOI instead. The API identified Hearne--Wagner,
+*Minimal Covers of Finite Sets* (1973), Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier, *Existence of
+Primitive Divisors of Lucas and Lehmer Numbers* (2001), and Renault, *The
+Period, Rank, and Order of the $(a,b)$-Fibonacci Sequence Mod $m$* (2013).
+
+The nearest combinatorial papers are Hearne--Wagner's enumeration of minimal
+covers, Royle's correspondence with split graphs, and the later split-graph
+asymptotics of Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka. The nearest arithmetic
+papers are Fulton--Morris and Lengyel on prime-power ranks, Bilu--Hanrot--
+Voutier on defective primitive-divisor indices, and Renault on the lcm rank
+identity for generalized Fibonacci sequences. The searches found no paper
+combining those inputs to classify the support sizes of minimal elements in a
+fixed Fibonacci apparition fiber, no extremal atomic-product formula, and no
+connected endpoint dichotomy involving the oriented defective rank $6$.
+
+Six candidates were compared on a five-point scale `(reach, novelty, value)`:
+
+- exact total/connected support spectra and the extremal slice: `(5,4,5)`;
+- exact realization criteria for covers meeting the even exceptional supports:
+  `(3,4,4)`;
+- support-refined polynomial connected-factorization identities: `(5,2,2)`;
+- transfer of the full witness-cover package to general Lucas sequences:
+  `(3,3,4)`;
+- complete connected four-coordinate kernel classification: `(2,4,4)`;
+- unconditional resolution of the rank-window sparsity alternatives:
+  `(1,5,5)`.
+
+The first candidate was selected. The third is a routine grading of the
+existing partition formula; the fourth needs a recurrence-specific atomic and
+defective-index analysis; the fifth is the manuscript's explicit high-support
+open project; and the sixth still needs arithmetic dispersion unavailable in
+the cited literature. The second remains plausible but requires a separate
+coprime slot classification for covers using ranks $2$, $6$, and $12$.

+def _rank_supports(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[frozenset, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-coordinate supports in the rank hypergraph."""
+    coordinates = prime_divisors(n)
+    supports = []
+    for prime, exponent in sorted(
+        (int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(m).items()
+    ):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime**exponent, n)
+        supports.append(
+            frozenset(i for i, ell in enumerate(coordinates) if rank % ell == 0)
+        )
+    return tuple(supports)
+
+
+def _supports_are_connected(supports: Sequence[frozenset], k: int) -> bool:
+    if k == 1:
+        return True
+    adjacency = [set() for _ in range(k)]
+    for support in supports:
+        for vertex in support:
+            adjacency[vertex].update(support - {vertex})
+    reached = {0}
+    frontier = [0]
+    while frontier:
+        vertex = frontier.pop()
+        for neighbor in adjacency[vertex] - reached:
+            reached.add(neighbor)
+            frontier.append(neighbor)
+    return len(reached) == k
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def support_spectra(n: int) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    """Compute the total and connected omega-spectra of M_n exactly."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    total = set()
+    connected = set()
+    for m in upper_fiber_threshold(n).minimal_generators:
+        size = omega(m)
+        total.add(size)
+        if _supports_are_connected(_rank_supports(m, n), k):
+            connected.add(size)
+    return tuple(sorted(total)), tuple(sorted(connected))
+
+
+def expected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted total support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    has_extremal_slice = not (2 in factors and all(e == 1 for e in factors.values()))
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+def expected_connected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted connected support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    if k == 1:
+        return (1,)
+    squarefree = all(e == 1 for e in factors.values())
+    rank_six_orientation_obstruction = (
+        factors.get(2) == 2
+        and factors.get(3) == 1
+        and all(e == 1 for p, e in factors.items() if p not in (2, 3))
+    )
+    has_connected_extremal_slice = (
+        not squarefree and not rank_six_orientation_obstruction
+    )
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_connected_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def extremal_support_product_count(n: int) -> int:
+    """Count the product of the k singleton diagonal atomic families."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("the extremal slice is stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    counts = [0] * k
+    for prime, top_exponent in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        for exponent in range(1, top_exponent + 1):
+            theta = prime**exponent
+            if alpha_for_fn_divisor(theta, n) == alpha_for_fn_divisor(
+                prime ** (exponent - 1), n
+            ):
+                continue
+            essential, full = _support_pairs(theta, n)[0]
+            if essential == full and len(full) == 1:
+                counts[next(iter(full))] += 1
+    return math.prod(counts)
+

+\begin{theorem}[Exact support spectra and the extremal slice]
+\label{thm:exact-support-spectra}
+Let $n\ge3$, write
+\[
+ n=\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\ell^{a_\ell},
+ \qquad k=\omega(n),
+\]
+and put
+\[
+ \Sigma(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n\},\qquad
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n^{\rm conn}\}.
+\]
+For each $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$, define the singleton diagonal atomic family
+\[
+ \mathcal A_\ell(n):=
+ \mathcal A_{\{\ell\},\{\ell\}}(n).
+\]
+Then multiplication gives a bijection
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection}
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\mathcal A_\ell(n)
+ \longrightarrow
+ \{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\},
+ \qquad (\theta_\ell)_\ell\longmapsto
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\theta_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+In particular,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-count}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\}
+ =\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\#\mathcal A_\ell(n).
+\end{equation}
+The complete support spectrum is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},&n\text{ is even and squarefree},\\
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+For the connected spectrum, $\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=\{1\}$ when $k=1$.
+If $k\ge2$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},
+   &\begin{array}{l}
+     n\text{ is squarefree, or }n=12s\text{ with }s\text{ squarefree}\
+     \text{and }\gcd(s,6)=1,
+    \end{array}\\[2mm]
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first classify the extremal slice. Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ have
+$\omega(m)=k$, and let $\Theta(m)$ be its witness cover. For every
+$\theta\in\Theta(m)$, choose a private coordinate
+\[
+ \ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
+ \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta(m),\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta).
+\]
+The chosen coordinates are distinct, since a coordinate chosen for two atoms
+would lie in the full support of each and hence would not be private to either.
+There are $k$ atoms and $k$ coordinates, so $\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a
+bijection. If $q\ne\ell(\theta)$, then $q$ is private to another atom and
+therefore cannot lie in $T_n(\theta)$. Hence
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=E_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}.
+\]
+Thus the inverse of \eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection} sends $m$
+to its uniquely labelled atoms in the families $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$.
+
+Conversely, choose $\theta_\ell\in\mathcal A_\ell(n)$ for every
+$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$.
+These atoms are pairwise coprime. Indeed, if
+$\theta_\ell=p^e$ and $\theta_q=p^f$ had the same underlying prime, then
+$e\ne f$ because the same atom cannot lie in two differently labelled
+families. Say $e<f$. Then $p^e\mid p^{f-1}$ would give
+\[
+ d(\theta_\ell)\mid d^-(\theta_q).
+\]
+Since $\ell$ occurs to its full $n$-adic exponent in $d(\theta_\ell)$, it
+would also occur fully in $d(\theta_q)$, contrary to
+$T_n(\theta_q)=\{q\}$ and $q\ne\ell$. The singleton full supports cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and the singleton essential supports are private. Hence the
+chosen atoms form an $n$-witness cover. The witness-cover theorem proves that
+their product belongs to $\mathcal M_n$ and has $k$ distinct prime factors.
+Uniqueness follows from unique factorization. This proves the bijection and
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count}.
+
+We next decide when the factors on the right of
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count} are nonzero. If $\ell$ is odd, or
+if $\ell=2$ and $a_2\ge2$, then the exact-rank existence theorem supplies a
+prime of rank $\ell^{a_\ell}$; this is an element of
+$\mathcal A_\ell(n)$. Suppose now that $a_2=1$. If $n$ is squarefree and
+$\theta\in\mathcal A_2(n)$, then $d(\theta)\mid n$ cannot contain an odd
+coordinate: every such coordinate would occur fully and would belong to
+$T_n(\theta)$. Thus $d(\theta)=2$, which is impossible because $F_2=1$ and
+$\Atom(2)=\varnothing$. Therefore the extremal slice is empty when $n$ is
+even and squarefree.
+
+If instead $a_2=1$ and $q^2\mid n$ for some odd prime $q$, take an atom of
+rank $2q$. For $q=3$, the atom $4\in\Atom(6)$ has, relative to $n$,
+$E_n(4)=T_n(4)=\{2\}$. For $q\ge5$, the rank $2q$ is nonexceptional, so an
+exact-rank prime exists and again has essential and full support $\{2\}$,
+because the $q$-coordinate is sub-full in $n$. Thus
+$\mathcal A_2(n)\ne\varnothing$. All other diagonal families were already
+seen to be nonempty, proving that the support value $k$ occurs exactly in the
+second case of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+It remains to realize every smaller support size. Assume $k\ge2$ and
+$1\le r\le k-1$. Choose a partition $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P(n)$ into $r$
+nonempty blocks, with the additional condition that $\{2\}$ is not a block
+when $a_2=1$. Such a partition exists because $r<k$. For $C\in\Pi$, put
+$n_C=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{a_\ell}$ and choose
+$\theta_C\in\Atom(n_C)$. This is possible by exact-rank prime existence
+unless $n_C\in\{6,12\}$; in those two cases use respectively
+$4\in\Atom(6)$ and $16\in\Atom(12)$. The forbidden rank $2$ was excluded by
+the choice of $\Pi$. Strong divisibility makes the atoms belonging to
+disjoint blocks pairwise coprime. Their full supports are the blocks $C$, and
+each has a nonempty essential support because lowering it decreases its rank.
+They therefore form an $n$-witness cover. Its product has exactly $r$ prime
+factors, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+The same idea gives all connected support sizes below $k$. Choose a hub
+$h\in\mathcal P(n)$, taking $h=3$ whenever
+$\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ and $n_{\{2,3\}}\in\{6,12\}$, and partition
+$\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{h\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.
+Use one atom of exact rank $n_{\{h\}\cup P_i}$ for each $i$. The only
+exceptional support that can occur is $\{2,3\}$; use $4$ at rank $6$ or $16$
+at rank $12$. In both cases its essential support contains the private
+coordinate $2\in P_i$. Every nonexceptional atom is a prime atom and has any
+coordinate of the nonempty set $P_i$ as a private coordinate. The atoms are
+pairwise coprime: their ranks are distinct, and the exceptional atom has
+underlying prime $2$, whose rank $3$ is not one of the other multi-coordinate
+ranks. The resulting witness cover is connected because all its rank-support
+edges contain $h$. Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}
+ \{1,\ldots,k-1\}\subseteq\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)\qquad(k\ge2).
+\end{equation}
+
+We finally decide whether the endpoint $k$ can be connected. In an extremal
+witness cover, write $\theta_\ell$ for the atom with
+$T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}$ and let
+$S_\ell=\operatorname{supp}_n(d(\theta_\ell))$ be its positive-coordinate
+rank support. If $q\in S_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}$, then
+\[
+ 1\le\nu_q(d(\theta_\ell))<a_q,
+\]
+so necessarily $a_q\ge2$. If $n$ is squarefree, every $S_\ell$ is therefore
+the singleton $\{\ell\}$, and the rank-support hypergraph is disconnected
+when $k\ge2$.
+
+There is one further obstruction. Let $n=12s$ with $s$ squarefree and
+$\gcd(s,6)=1$. The only coordinate of exponent at least two is $2$. Hence an
+edge $S_3$ larger than $\{3\}$ would force $d(\theta_3)=6$. But
+$\Atom(6)=\{4\}$, and lowering $4$ gives rank $3$; relative to this $n$, the
+$3$-coordinate is not lost. Thus an atom of rank $6$ with
+$T_n(\theta_3)=\{3\}$ has empty essential support and cannot occur in a
+witness cover. Consequently $S_3=\{3\}$. Since $a_3=1$, the coordinate $3$
+cannot occur sub-fully in any other $S_\ell$, so it is isolated and the
+extremal generator is disconnected.
+
+Conversely, suppose that $n$ is nonsquarefree and is not of the preceding
+form. Choose a coordinate $h$ with $a_h\ge2$. If possible take $h\ne2$. For
+each $\ell\ne h$, choose an atom of rank
+\[
+ d_\ell=\ell^{a_\ell}h,
+\]
+and choose an exact-rank prime of rank $h^{a_h}$ for the $h$-atom. The ranks
+$d_\ell$ are nonexceptional except possibly when $h=3$ and $\ell=2$; use
+$4$ when $d_2=6$ and $16$ when $d_2=12$. These exceptional atoms have
+$E_n=T_n=\{2\}$ because the $3$-coordinate is sub-full. If the only possible
+hub is $h=2$, then either $3\nmid n$ or $a_2\ge3$. In the latter case, use
+$9\in\Atom(12)$ for the $3$-atom; relative to $n$ it has
+$E_n(9)=T_n(9)=\{3\}$. Use exact-rank primes of rank
+$\ell^{a_\ell}2$ for the remaining nonhub coordinates. In every case we have
+chosen one atom from each $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$, so the extremal-slice
+bijection makes their product a minimal generator. Its rank-support edges are
+$\{h\}$ and the pairs $\{h,\ell\}$, hence it is connected. Together with
+\eqref{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}, this proves
+\eqref{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound-sharp}
+For $n\ge3$, there exists $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with
+$\omega(m)=\omega(n)$ if and only if $n$ is not even and squarefree. In
+particular, equality occurs on every odd layer.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+This is the endpoint assertion in \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}

 - `thm:minimal-generator-growth`: new headline arithmetic result. With `k=omega(n)` and `R(n)` the largest atomic rank-window multiplicity, it proves the sharp private-coordinate bounds `(2^floor(k/2)-1)^ceil(k/2) <= #M_n <= sum_{s<=k} binom(k,s)(2R(n))^s 2^{s(k-s)}` for `k>=3`. It gives the unconditional mean lower bound `(log 2/4+o(1))x(log log x)^2`, and exact normal and mean orders under explicit rank-window sparsity hypotheses. +## Deep Exploration Check: Exact Support Spectra
+
+Checked 2026-08-08. Fresh queries were sent to the arXiv Atom API, Crossref,
+Semantic Scholar, and zbMATH Open for Fibonacci ranks of apparition, minimal
+generators, minimal covers, connected hypergraphs, split graphs, primitive
+divisors, and strong divisibility sequences. Semantic Scholar's keyword-search
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 from the shared address, so the three nearest known
+papers were checked there by DOI instead. The API identified Hearne--Wagner,
+*Minimal Covers of Finite Sets* (1973), Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier, *Existence of
+Primitive Divisors of Lucas and Lehmer Numbers* (2001), and Renault, *The
+Period, Rank, and Order of the $(a,b)$-Fibonacci Sequence Mod $m$* (2013).
+
+The nearest combinatorial papers are Hearne--Wagner's enumeration of minimal
+covers, Royle's correspondence with split graphs, and the later split-graph
+asymptotics of Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka. The nearest arithmetic
+papers are Fulton--Morris and Lengyel on prime-power ranks, Bilu--Hanrot--
+Voutier on defective primitive-divisor indices, and Renault on the lcm rank
+identity for generalized Fibonacci sequences. The searches found no paper
+combining those inputs to classify the support sizes of minimal elements in a
+fixed Fibonacci apparition fiber, no extremal atomic-product formula, and no
+connected endpoint dichotomy involving the oriented defective rank $6$.
+
+Six candidates were compared on a five-point scale `(reach, novelty, value)`:
+
+- exact total/connected support spectra and the extremal slice: `(5,4,5)`;
+- exact realization criteria for covers meeting the even exceptional supports:
+  `(3,4,4)`;
+- support-refined polynomial connected-factorization identities: `(5,2,2)`;
+- transfer of the full witness-cover package to general Lucas sequences:
+  `(3,3,4)`;
+- complete connected four-coordinate kernel classification: `(2,4,4)`;
+- unconditional resolution of the rank-window sparsity alternatives:
+  `(1,5,5)`.
+
+The first candidate was selected. The third is a routine grading of the
+existing partition formula; the fourth needs a recurrence-specific atomic and
+defective-index analysis; the fifth is the manuscript's explicit high-support
+open project; and the sixth still needs arithmetic dispersion unavailable in
+the cited literature. The second remains plausible but requires a separate
+coprime slot classification for covers using ranks $2$, $6$, and $12$.

+def _rank_supports(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[frozenset, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-coordinate supports in the rank hypergraph."""
+    coordinates = prime_divisors(n)
+    supports = []
+    for prime, exponent in sorted(
+        (int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(m).items()
+    ):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime**exponent, n)
+        supports.append(
+            frozenset(i for i, ell in enumerate(coordinates) if rank % ell == 0)
+        )
+    return tuple(supports)
+
+
+def _supports_are_connected(supports: Sequence[frozenset], k: int) -> bool:
+    if k == 1:
+        return True
+    adjacency = [set() for _ in range(k)]
+    for support in supports:
+        for vertex in support:
+            adjacency[vertex].update(support - {vertex})
+    reached = {0}
+    frontier = [0]
+    while frontier:
+        vertex = frontier.pop()
+        for neighbor in adjacency[vertex] - reached:
+            reached.add(neighbor)
+            frontier.append(neighbor)
+    return len(reached) == k
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def support_spectra(n: int) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    """Compute the total and connected omega-spectra of M_n exactly."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    total = set()
+    connected = set()
+    for m in upper_fiber_threshold(n).minimal_generators:
+        size = omega(m)
+        total.add(size)
+        if _supports_are_connected(_rank_supports(m, n), k):
+            connected.add(size)
+    return tuple(sorted(total)), tuple(sorted(connected))
+
+
+def expected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted total support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    has_extremal_slice = not (2 in factors and all(e == 1 for e in factors.values()))
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+def expected_connected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted connected support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    if k == 1:
+        return (1,)
+    squarefree = all(e == 1 for e in factors.values())
+    rank_six_orientation_obstruction = (
+        factors.get(2) == 2
+        and factors.get(3) == 1
+        and all(e == 1 for p, e in factors.items() if p not in (2, 3))
+    )
+    has_connected_extremal_slice = (
+        not squarefree and not rank_six_orientation_obstruction
+    )
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_connected_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def extremal_support_product_count(n: int) -> int:
+    """Count the product of the k singleton diagonal atomic families."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("the extremal slice is stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    counts = [0] * k
+    for prime, top_exponent in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        for exponent in range(1, top_exponent + 1):
+            theta = prime**exponent
+            if alpha_for_fn_divisor(theta, n) == alpha_for_fn_divisor(
+                prime ** (exponent - 1), n
+            ):
+                continue
+            essential, full = _support_pairs(theta, n)[0]
+            if essential == full and len(full) == 1:
+                counts[next(iter(full))] += 1
+    return math.prod(counts)
+

+\begin{theorem}[Exact support spectra and the extremal slice]
+\label{thm:exact-support-spectra}
+Let $n\ge3$, write
+\[
+ n=\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\ell^{a_\ell},
+ \qquad k=\omega(n),
+\]
+and put
+\[
+ \Sigma(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n\},\qquad
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n^{\rm conn}\}.
+\]
+For each $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$, define the singleton diagonal atomic family
+\[
+ \mathcal A_\ell(n):=
+ \mathcal A_{\{\ell\},\{\ell\}}(n).
+\]
+Then multiplication gives a bijection
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection}
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\mathcal A_\ell(n)
+ \longrightarrow
+ \{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\},
+ \qquad (\theta_\ell)_\ell\longmapsto
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\theta_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+In particular,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-count}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\}
+ =\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\#\mathcal A_\ell(n).
+\end{equation}
+The complete support spectrum is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},&n\text{ is even and squarefree},\\
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+For the connected spectrum, $\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=\{1\}$ when $k=1$.
+If $k\ge2$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},
+   &\begin{array}{l}
+     n\text{ is squarefree, or }n=12s\text{ with }s\text{ squarefree}\
+     \text{and }\gcd(s,6)=1,
+    \end{array}\\[2mm]
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first classify the extremal slice. Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ have
+$\omega(m)=k$, and let $\Theta(m)$ be its witness cover. For every
+$\theta\in\Theta(m)$, choose a private coordinate
+\[
+ \ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
+ \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta(m),\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta).
+\]
+The chosen coordinates are distinct, since a coordinate chosen for two atoms
+would lie in the full support of each and hence would not be private to either.
+There are $k$ atoms and $k$ coordinates, so $\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a
+bijection. If $q\ne\ell(\theta)$, then $q$ is private to another atom and
+therefore cannot lie in $T_n(\theta)$. Hence
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=E_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}.
+\]
+Thus the inverse of \eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection} sends $m$
+to its uniquely labelled atoms in the families $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$.
+
+Conversely, choose $\theta_\ell\in\mathcal A_\ell(n)$ for every
+$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$.
+These atoms are pairwise coprime. Indeed, if
+$\theta_\ell=p^e$ and $\theta_q=p^f$ had the same underlying prime, then
+$e\ne f$ because the same atom cannot lie in two differently labelled
+families. Say $e<f$. Then $p^e\mid p^{f-1}$ would give
+\[
+ d(\theta_\ell)\mid d^-(\theta_q).
+\]
+Since $\ell$ occurs to its full $n$-adic exponent in $d(\theta_\ell)$, it
+would also occur fully in $d(\theta_q)$, contrary to
+$T_n(\theta_q)=\{q\}$ and $q\ne\ell$. The singleton full supports cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and the singleton essential supports are private. Hence the
+chosen atoms form an $n$-witness cover. The witness-cover theorem proves that
+their product belongs to $\mathcal M_n$ and has $k$ distinct prime factors.
+Uniqueness follows from unique factorization. This proves the bijection and
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count}.
+
+We next decide when the factors on the right of
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count} are nonzero. If $\ell$ is odd, or
+if $\ell=2$ and $a_2\ge2$, then the exact-rank existence theorem supplies a
+prime of rank $\ell^{a_\ell}$; this is an element of
+$\mathcal A_\ell(n)$. Suppose now that $a_2=1$. If $n$ is squarefree and
+$\theta\in\mathcal A_2(n)$, then $d(\theta)\mid n$ cannot contain an odd
+coordinate: every such coordinate would occur fully and would belong to
+$T_n(\theta)$. Thus $d(\theta)=2$, which is impossible because $F_2=1$ and
+$\Atom(2)=\varnothing$. Therefore the extremal slice is empty when $n$ is
+even and squarefree.
+
+If instead $a_2=1$ and $q^2\mid n$ for some odd prime $q$, take an atom of
+rank $2q$. For $q=3$, the atom $4\in\Atom(6)$ has, relative to $n$,
+$E_n(4)=T_n(4)=\{2\}$. For $q\ge5$, the rank $2q$ is nonexceptional, so an
+exact-rank prime exists and again has essential and full support $\{2\}$,
+because the $q$-coordinate is sub-full in $n$. Thus
+$\mathcal A_2(n)\ne\varnothing$. All other diagonal families were already
+seen to be nonempty, proving that the support value $k$ occurs exactly in the
+second case of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+It remains to realize every smaller support size. Assume $k\ge2$ and
+$1\le r\le k-1$. Choose a partition $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P(n)$ into $r$
+nonempty blocks, with the additional condition that $\{2\}$ is not a block
+when $a_2=1$. Such a partition exists because $r<k$. For $C\in\Pi$, put
+$n_C=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{a_\ell}$ and choose
+$\theta_C\in\Atom(n_C)$. This is possible by exact-rank prime existence
+unless $n_C\in\{6,12\}$; in those two cases use respectively
+$4\in\Atom(6)$ and $16\in\Atom(12)$. The forbidden rank $2$ was excluded by
+the choice of $\Pi$. Strong divisibility makes the atoms belonging to
+disjoint blocks pairwise coprime. Their full supports are the blocks $C$, and
+each has a nonempty essential support because lowering it decreases its rank.
+They therefore form an $n$-witness cover. Its product has exactly $r$ prime
+factors, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+The same idea gives all connected support sizes below $k$. Choose a hub
+$h\in\mathcal P(n)$, taking $h=3$ whenever
+$\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ and $n_{\{2,3\}}\in\{6,12\}$, and partition
+$\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{h\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.
+Use one atom of exact rank $n_{\{h\}\cup P_i}$ for each $i$. The only
+exceptional support that can occur is $\{2,3\}$; use $4$ at rank $6$ or $16$
+at rank $12$. In both cases its essential support contains the private
+coordinate $2\in P_i$. Every nonexceptional atom is a prime atom and has any
+coordinate of the nonempty set $P_i$ as a private coordinate. The atoms are
+pairwise coprime: their ranks are distinct, and the exceptional atom has
+underlying prime $2$, whose rank $3$ is not one of the other multi-coordinate
+ranks. The resulting witness cover is connected because all its rank-support
+edges contain $h$. Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}
+ \{1,\ldots,k-1\}\subseteq\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)\qquad(k\ge2).
+\end{equation}
+
+We finally decide whether the endpoint $k$ can be connected. In an extremal
+witness cover, write $\theta_\ell$ for the atom with
+$T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}$ and let
+$S_\ell=\operatorname{supp}_n(d(\theta_\ell))$ be its positive-coordinate
+rank support. If $q\in S_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}$, then
+\[
+ 1\le\nu_q(d(\theta_\ell))<a_q,
+\]
+so necessarily $a_q\ge2$. If $n$ is squarefree, every $S_\ell$ is therefore
+the singleton $\{\ell\}$, and the rank-support hypergraph is disconnected
+when $k\ge2$.
+
+There is one further obstruction. Let $n=12s$ with $s$ squarefree and
+$\gcd(s,6)=1$. The only coordinate of exponent at least two is $2$. Hence an
+edge $S_3$ larger than $\{3\}$ would force $d(\theta_3)=6$. But
+$\Atom(6)=\{4\}$, and lowering $4$ gives rank $3$; relative to this $n$, the
+$3$-coordinate is not lost. Thus an atom of rank $6$ with
+$T_n(\theta_3)=\{3\}$ has empty essential support and cannot occur in a
+witness cover. Consequently $S_3=\{3\}$. Since $a_3=1$, the coordinate $3$
+cannot occur sub-fully in any other $S_\ell$, so it is isolated and the
+extremal generator is disconnected.
+
+Conversely, suppose that $n$ is nonsquarefree and is not of the preceding
+form. Choose a coordinate $h$ with $a_h\ge2$. If possible take $h\ne2$. For
+each $\ell\ne h$, choose an atom of rank
+\[
+ d_\ell=\ell^{a_\ell}h,
+\]
+and choose an exact-rank prime of rank $h^{a_h}$ for the $h$-atom. The ranks
+$d_\ell$ are nonexceptional except possibly when $h=3$ and $\ell=2$; use
+$4$ when $d_2=6$ and $16$ when $d_2=12$. These exceptional atoms have
+$E_n=T_n=\{2\}$ because the $3$-coordinate is sub-full. If the only possible
+hub is $h=2$, then either $3\nmid n$ or $a_2\ge3$. In the latter case, use
+$9\in\Atom(12)$ for the $3$-atom; relative to $n$ it has
+$E_n(9)=T_n(9)=\{3\}$. Use exact-rank primes of rank
+$\ell^{a_\ell}2$ for the remaining nonhub coordinates. In every case we have
+chosen one atom from each $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$, so the extremal-slice
+bijection makes their product a minimal generator. Its rank-support edges are
+$\{h\}$ and the pairs $\{h,\ell\}$, hence it is connected. Together with
+\eqref{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}, this proves
+\eqref{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound-sharp}
+For $n\ge3$, there exists $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with
+$\omega(m)=\omega(n)$ if and only if $n$ is not even and squarefree. In
+particular, equality occurs on every odd layer.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+This is the endpoint assertion in \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}

+## Deep Exploration Check: Exact Support Spectra
+
+Checked 2026-08-08. Fresh queries were sent to the arXiv Atom API, Crossref,
+Semantic Scholar, and zbMATH Open for Fibonacci ranks of apparition, minimal
+generators, minimal covers, connected hypergraphs, split graphs, primitive
+divisors, and strong divisibility sequences. Semantic Scholar's keyword-search
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 from the shared address, so the three nearest known
+papers were checked there by DOI instead. The API identified Hearne--Wagner,
+*Minimal Covers of Finite Sets* (1973), Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier, *Existence of
+Primitive Divisors of Lucas and Lehmer Numbers* (2001), and Renault, *The
+Period, Rank, and Order of the $(a,b)$-Fibonacci Sequence Mod $m$* (2013).
+
+The nearest combinatorial papers are Hearne--Wagner's enumeration of minimal
+covers, Royle's correspondence with split graphs, and the later split-graph
+asymptotics of Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka. The nearest arithmetic
+papers are Fulton--Morris and Lengyel on prime-power ranks, Bilu--Hanrot--
+Voutier on defective primitive-divisor indices, and Renault on the lcm rank
+identity for generalized Fibonacci sequences. The searches found no paper
+combining those inputs to classify the support sizes of minimal elements in a
+fixed Fibonacci apparition fiber, no extremal atomic-product formula, and no
+connected endpoint dichotomy involving the oriented defective rank $6$.
+
+Six candidates were compared on a five-point scale `(reach, novelty, value)`:
+
+- exact total/connected support spectra and the extremal slice: `(5,4,5)`;
+- exact realization criteria for covers meeting the even exceptional supports:
+  `(3,4,4)`;
+- support-refined polynomial connected-factorization identities: `(5,2,2)`;
+- transfer of the full witness-cover package to general Lucas sequences:
+  `(3,3,4)`;
+- complete connected four-coordinate kernel classification: `(2,4,4)`;
+- unconditional resolution of the rank-window sparsity alternatives:
+  `(1,5,5)`.
+
+The first candidate was selected. The third is a routine grading of the
+existing partition formula; the fourth needs a recurrence-specific atomic and
+defective-index analysis; the fifth is the manuscript's explicit high-support
+open project; and the sixth still needs arithmetic dispersion unavailable in
+the cited literature. The second remains plausible but requires a separate
+coprime slot classification for covers using ranks $2$, $6$, and $12$.

+def _rank_supports(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[frozenset, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-coordinate supports in the rank hypergraph."""
+    coordinates = prime_divisors(n)
+    supports = []
+    for prime, exponent in sorted(
+        (int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(m).items()
+    ):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime**exponent, n)
+        supports.append(
+            frozenset(i for i, ell in enumerate(coordinates) if rank % ell == 0)
+        )
+    return tuple(supports)
+
+
+def _supports_are_connected(supports: Sequence[frozenset], k: int) -> bool:
+    if k == 1:
+        return True
+    adjacency = [set() for _ in range(k)]
+    for support in supports:
+        for vertex in support:
+            adjacency[vertex].update(support - {vertex})
+    reached = {0}
+    frontier = [0]
+    while frontier:
+        vertex = frontier.pop()
+        for neighbor in adjacency[vertex] - reached:
+            reached.add(neighbor)
+            frontier.append(neighbor)
+    return len(reached) == k
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def support_spectra(n: int) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    """Compute the total and connected omega-spectra of M_n exactly."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    total = set()
+    connected = set()
+    for m in upper_fiber_threshold(n).minimal_generators:
+        size = omega(m)
+        total.add(size)
+        if _supports_are_connected(_rank_supports(m, n), k):
+            connected.add(size)
+    return tuple(sorted(total)), tuple(sorted(connected))
+
+
+def expected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted total support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    has_extremal_slice = not (2 in factors and all(e == 1 for e in factors.values()))
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+def expected_connected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted connected support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    if k == 1:
+        return (1,)
+    squarefree = all(e == 1 for e in factors.values())
+    rank_six_orientation_obstruction = (
+        factors.get(2) == 2
+        and factors.get(3) == 1
+        and all(e == 1 for p, e in factors.items() if p not in (2, 3))
+    )
+    has_connected_extremal_slice = (
+        not squarefree and not rank_six_orientation_obstruction
+    )
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_connected_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def extremal_support_product_count(n: int) -> int:
+    """Count the product of the k singleton diagonal atomic families."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("the extremal slice is stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    counts = [0] * k
+    for prime, top_exponent in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        for exponent in range(1, top_exponent + 1):
+            theta = prime**exponent
+            if alpha_for_fn_divisor(theta, n) == alpha_for_fn_divisor(
+                prime ** (exponent - 1), n
+            ):
+                continue
+            essential, full = _support_pairs(theta, n)[0]
+            if essential == full and len(full) == 1:
+                counts[next(iter(full))] += 1
+    return math.prod(counts)

+\begin{theorem}[Exact support spectra and the extremal slice]
+\label{thm:exact-support-spectra}
+Let $n\ge3$, write
+\[
+ n=\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\ell^{a_\ell},
+ \qquad k=\omega(n),
+\]
+and put
+\[
+ \Sigma(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n\},\qquad
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n^{\rm conn}\}.
+\]
+For each $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$, define the singleton diagonal atomic family
+\[
+ \mathcal A_\ell(n):=
+ \mathcal A_{\{\ell\},\{\ell\}}(n).
+\]
+Then multiplication gives a bijection
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection}
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\mathcal A_\ell(n)
+ \longrightarrow
+ \{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\},
+ \qquad (\theta_\ell)_\ell\longmapsto
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\theta_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+In particular,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-count}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\}
+ =\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\#\mathcal A_\ell(n).
+\end{equation}
+The complete support spectrum is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},&n\text{ is even and squarefree},\\
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+For the connected spectrum, $\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=\{1\}$ when $k=1$.
+If $k\ge2$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},
+   &\begin{array}{l}
+     n\text{ is squarefree, or }n=12s\text{ with }s\text{ squarefree}\
+     \text{and }\gcd(s,6)=1,
+    \end{array}\\[2mm]
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first classify the extremal slice. Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ have
+$\omega(m)=k$, and let $\Theta(m)$ be its witness cover. For every
+$\theta\in\Theta(m)$, choose a private coordinate
+\[
+ \ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
+ \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta(m),\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta).
+\]
+The chosen coordinates are distinct, since a coordinate chosen for two atoms
+would lie in the full support of each and hence would not be private to either.
+There are $k$ atoms and $k$ coordinates, so $\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a
+bijection. If $q\ne\ell(\theta)$, then $q$ is private to another atom and
+therefore cannot lie in $T_n(\theta)$. Hence
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=E_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}.
+\]
+Thus the inverse of \eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection} sends $m$
+to its uniquely labelled atoms in the families $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$.
+
+Conversely, choose $\theta_\ell\in\mathcal A_\ell(n)$ for every
+$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$.
+These atoms are pairwise coprime. Indeed, if
+$\theta_\ell=p^e$ and $\theta_q=p^f$ had the same underlying prime, then
+$e\ne f$ because the same atom cannot lie in two differently labelled
+families. Say $e<f$. Then $p^e\mid p^{f-1}$ would give
+\[
+ d(\theta_\ell)\mid d^-(\theta_q).
+\]
+Since $\ell$ occurs to its full $n$-adic exponent in $d(\theta_\ell)$, it
+would also occur fully in $d(\theta_q)$, contrary to
+$T_n(\theta_q)=\{q\}$ and $q\ne\ell$. The singleton full supports cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and the singleton essential supports are private. Hence the
+chosen atoms form an $n$-witness cover. The witness-cover theorem proves that
+their product belongs to $\mathcal M_n$ and has $k$ distinct prime factors.
+Uniqueness follows from unique factorization. This proves the bijection and
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count}.
+
+We next decide when the factors on the right of
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count} are nonzero. If $\ell$ is odd, or
+if $\ell=2$ and $a_2\ge2$, then the exact-rank existence theorem supplies a
+prime of rank $\ell^{a_\ell}$; this is an element of
+$\mathcal A_\ell(n)$. Suppose now that $a_2=1$. If $n$ is squarefree and
+$\theta\in\mathcal A_2(n)$, then $d(\theta)\mid n$ cannot contain an odd
+coordinate: every such coordinate would occur fully and would belong to
+$T_n(\theta)$. Thus $d(\theta)=2$, which is impossible because $F_2=1$ and
+$\Atom(2)=\varnothing$. Therefore the extremal slice is empty when $n$ is
+even and squarefree.
+
+If instead $a_2=1$ and $q^2\mid n$ for some odd prime $q$, take an atom of
+rank $2q$. For $q=3$, the atom $4\in\Atom(6)$ has, relative to $n$,
+$E_n(4)=T_n(4)=\{2\}$. For $q\ge5$, the rank $2q$ is nonexceptional, so an
+exact-rank prime exists and again has essential and full support $\{2\}$,
+because the $q$-coordinate is sub-full in $n$. Thus
+$\mathcal A_2(n)\ne\varnothing$. All other diagonal families were already
+seen to be nonempty, proving that the support value $k$ occurs exactly in the
+second case of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+It remains to realize every smaller support size. Assume $k\ge2$ and
+$1\le r\le k-1$. Choose a partition $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P(n)$ into $r$
+nonempty blocks, with the additional condition that $\{2\}$ is not a block
+when $a_2=1$. Such a partition exists because $r<k$. For $C\in\Pi$, put
+$n_C=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{a_\ell}$ and choose
+$\theta_C\in\Atom(n_C)$. This is possible by exact-rank prime existence
+unless $n_C\in\{6,12\}$; in those two cases use respectively
+$4\in\Atom(6)$ and $16\in\Atom(12)$. The forbidden rank $2$ was excluded by
+the choice of $\Pi$. Strong divisibility makes the atoms belonging to
+disjoint blocks pairwise coprime. Their full supports are the blocks $C$, and
+each has a nonempty essential support because lowering it decreases its rank.
+They therefore form an $n$-witness cover. Its product has exactly $r$ prime
+factors, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+The same idea gives all connected support sizes below $k$. Choose a hub
+$h\in\mathcal P(n)$, taking $h=3$ whenever
+$\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ and $n_{\{2,3\}}\in\{6,12\}$, and partition
+$\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{h\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.
+Use one atom of exact rank $n_{\{h\}\cup P_i}$ for each $i$. The only
+exceptional support that can occur is $\{2,3\}$; use $4$ at rank $6$ or $16$
+at rank $12$. In both cases its essential support contains the private
+coordinate $2\in P_i$. Every nonexceptional atom is a prime atom and has any
+coordinate of the nonempty set $P_i$ as a private coordinate. The atoms are
+pairwise coprime: their ranks are distinct, and the exceptional atom has
+underlying prime $2$, whose rank $3$ is not one of the other multi-coordinate
+ranks. The resulting witness cover is connected because all its rank-support
+edges contain $h$. Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}
+ \{1,\ldots,k-1\}\subseteq\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)\qquad(k\ge2).
+\end{equation}
+
+We finally decide whether the endpoint $k$ can be connected. In an extremal
+witness cover, write $\theta_\ell$ for the atom with
+$T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}$ and let
+$S_\ell=\operatorname{supp}_n(d(\theta_\ell))$ be its positive-coordinate
+rank support. If $q\in S_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}$, then
+\[
+ 1\le\nu_q(d(\theta_\ell))<a_q,
+\]
+so necessarily $a_q\ge2$. If $n$ is squarefree, every $S_\ell$ is therefore
+the singleton $\{\ell\}$, and the rank-support hypergraph is disconnected
+when $k\ge2$.
+
+There is one further obstruction. Let $n=12s$ with $s$ squarefree and
+$\gcd(s,6)=1$. The only coordinate of exponent at least two is $2$. Hence an
+edge $S_3$ larger than $\{3\}$ would force $d(\theta_3)=6$. But
+$\Atom(6)=\{4\}$, and lowering $4$ gives rank $3$; relative to this $n$, the
+$3$-coordinate is not lost. Thus an atom of rank $6$ with
+$T_n(\theta_3)=\{3\}$ has empty essential support and cannot occur in a
+witness cover. Consequently $S_3=\{3\}$. Since $a_3=1$, the coordinate $3$
+cannot occur sub-fully in any other $S_\ell$, so it is isolated and the
+extremal generator is disconnected.
+
+Conversely, suppose that $n$ is nonsquarefree and is not of the preceding
+form. Choose a coordinate $h$ with $a_h\ge2$. If possible take $h\ne2$. For
+each $\ell\ne h$, choose an atom of rank
+\[
+ d_\ell=\ell^{a_\ell}h,
+\]
+and choose an exact-rank prime of rank $h^{a_h}$ for the $h$-atom. The ranks
+$d_\ell$ are nonexceptional except possibly when $h=3$ and $\ell=2$; use
+$4$ when $d_2=6$ and $16$ when $d_2=12$. These exceptional atoms have
+$E_n=T_n=\{2\}$ because the $3$-coordinate is sub-full. If the only possible
+hub is $h=2$, then either $3\nmid n$ or $a_2\ge3$. In the latter case, use
+$9\in\Atom(12)$ for the $3$-atom; relative to $n$ it has
+$E_n(9)=T_n(9)=\{3\}$. Use exact-rank primes of rank
+$\ell^{a_\ell}2$ for the remaining nonhub coordinates. In every case we have
+chosen one atom from each $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$, so the extremal-slice
+bijection makes their product a minimal generator. Its rank-support edges are
+$\{h\}$ and the pairs $\{h,\ell\}$, hence it is connected. Together with
+\eqref{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}, this proves
+\eqref{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound-sharp}
+For $n\ge3$, there exists $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with
+$\omega(m)=\omega(n)$ if and only if $n$ is not even and squarefree. In
+particular, equality occurs on every odd layer.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+This is the endpoint assertion in \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}

+## Deep Exploration Check: Exact Support Spectra
+
+Checked 2026-08-08. Fresh queries were sent to the arXiv Atom API, Crossref,
+Semantic Scholar, and zbMATH Open for Fibonacci ranks of apparition, minimal
+generators, minimal covers, connected hypergraphs, split graphs, primitive
+divisors, and strong divisibility sequences. Semantic Scholar's keyword-search
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 from the shared address, so the three nearest known
+papers were checked there by DOI instead. The API identified Hearne--Wagner,
+*Minimal Covers of Finite Sets* (1973), Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier, *Existence of
+Primitive Divisors of Lucas and Lehmer Numbers* (2001), and Renault, *The
+Period, Rank, and Order of the $(a,b)$-Fibonacci Sequence Mod $m$* (2013).
+
+The nearest combinatorial papers are Hearne--Wagner's enumeration of minimal
+covers, Royle's correspondence with split graphs, and the later split-graph
+asymptotics of Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka. The nearest arithmetic
+papers are Fulton--Morris and Lengyel on prime-power ranks, Bilu--Hanrot--
+Voutier on defective primitive-divisor indices, and Renault on the lcm rank
+identity for generalized Fibonacci sequences. The searches found no paper
+combining those inputs to classify the support sizes of minimal elements in a
+fixed Fibonacci apparition fiber, no extremal atomic-product formula, and no
+connected endpoint dichotomy involving the oriented defective rank $6$.
+
+Six candidates were compared on a five-point scale `(reach, novelty, value)`:
+
+- exact total/connected support spectra and the extremal slice: `(5,4,5)`;
+- exact realization criteria for covers meeting the even exceptional supports:
+  `(3,4,4)`;
+- support-refined polynomial connected-factorization identities: `(5,2,2)`;
+- transfer of the full witness-cover package to general Lucas sequences:
+  `(3,3,4)`;
+- complete connected four-coordinate kernel classification: `(2,4,4)`;
+- unconditional resolution of the rank-window sparsity alternatives:
+  `(1,5,5)`.
+
+The first candidate was selected. The third is a routine grading of the
+existing partition formula; the fourth needs a recurrence-specific atomic and
+defective-index analysis; the fifth is the manuscript's explicit high-support
+open project; and the sixth still needs arithmetic dispersion unavailable in
+the cited literature. The second remains plausible but requires a separate
+coprime slot classification for covers using ranks $2$, $6$, and $12$.

+def _rank_supports(m: int, n: int) -> Tuple[frozenset, ...]:
+    """Return the positive-coordinate supports in the rank hypergraph."""
+    coordinates = prime_divisors(n)
+    supports = []
+    for prime, exponent in sorted(
+        (int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(m).items()
+    ):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime**exponent, n)
+        supports.append(
+            frozenset(i for i, ell in enumerate(coordinates) if rank % ell == 0)
+        )
+    return tuple(supports)
+
+
+def _supports_are_connected(supports: Sequence[frozenset], k: int) -> bool:
+    if k == 1:
+        return True
+    adjacency = [set() for _ in range(k)]
+    for support in supports:
+        for vertex in support:
+            adjacency[vertex].update(support - {vertex})
+    reached = {0}
+    frontier = [0]
+    while frontier:
+        vertex = frontier.pop()
+        for neighbor in adjacency[vertex] - reached:
+            reached.add(neighbor)
+            frontier.append(neighbor)
+    return len(reached) == k
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def support_spectra(n: int) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, ...], Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    """Compute the total and connected omega-spectra of M_n exactly."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    total = set()
+    connected = set()
+    for m in upper_fiber_threshold(n).minimal_generators:
+        size = omega(m)
+        total.add(size)
+        if _supports_are_connected(_rank_supports(m, n), k):
+            connected.add(size)
+    return tuple(sorted(total)), tuple(sorted(connected))
+
+
+def expected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted total support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    has_extremal_slice = not (2 in factors and all(e == 1 for e in factors.values()))
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+def expected_connected_support_spectrum(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the theorem's predicted connected support spectrum."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("support spectra are stated here only for n >= 3")
+    factors = factor_dict(
+        tuple(sorted((int(p), int(e)) for p, e in factorint(n).items()))
+    )
+    k = len(factors)
+    if k == 1:
+        return (1,)
+    squarefree = all(e == 1 for e in factors.values())
+    rank_six_orientation_obstruction = (
+        factors.get(2) == 2
+        and factors.get(3) == 1
+        and all(e == 1 for p, e in factors.items() if p not in (2, 3))
+    )
+    has_connected_extremal_slice = (
+        not squarefree and not rank_six_orientation_obstruction
+    )
+    return tuple(range(1, k + 1 if has_connected_extremal_slice else k))
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
+def extremal_support_product_count(n: int) -> int:
+    """Count the product of the k singleton diagonal atomic families."""
+    if n < 3:
+        raise ValueError("the extremal slice is stated here only for n >= 3")
+    k = omega(n)
+    counts = [0] * k
+    for prime, top_exponent in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        for exponent in range(1, top_exponent + 1):
+            theta = prime**exponent
+            if alpha_for_fn_divisor(theta, n) == alpha_for_fn_divisor(
+                prime ** (exponent - 1), n
+            ):
+                continue
+            essential, full = _support_pairs(theta, n)[0]
+            if essential == full and len(full) == 1:
+                counts[next(iter(full))] += 1
+    return math.prod(counts)
+

+\begin{theorem}[Exact support spectra and the extremal slice]
+\label{thm:exact-support-spectra}
+Let $n\ge3$, write
+\[
+ n=\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\ell^{a_\ell},
+ \qquad k=\omega(n),
+\]
+and put
+\[
+ \Sigma(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n\},\qquad
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n):=\{\omega(m):m\in\mathcal M_n^{\rm conn}\}.
+\]
+For each $\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$, define the singleton diagonal atomic family
+\[
+ \mathcal A_\ell(n):=
+ \mathcal A_{\{\ell\},\{\ell\}}(n).
+\]
+Then multiplication gives a bijection
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection}
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\mathcal A_\ell(n)
+ \longrightarrow
+ \{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\},
+ \qquad (\theta_\ell)_\ell\longmapsto
+ \prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\theta_\ell.
+\end{equation}
+In particular,
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:extremal-support-product-count}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\omega(m)=k\}
+ =\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(n)}\#\mathcal A_\ell(n).
+\end{equation}
+The complete support spectrum is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},&n\text{ is even and squarefree},\\
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+For the connected spectrum, $\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=\{1\}$ when $k=1$.
+If $k\ge2$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}
+ \Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)=
+ \begin{cases}
+  \{1,\ldots,k-1\},
+   &\begin{array}{l}
+     n\text{ is squarefree, or }n=12s\text{ with }s\text{ squarefree}\
+     \text{and }\gcd(s,6)=1,
+    \end{array}\\[2mm]
+  \{1,\ldots,k\},&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\end{equation}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We first classify the extremal slice. Let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ have
+$\omega(m)=k$, and let $\Theta(m)$ be its witness cover. For every
+$\theta\in\Theta(m)$, choose a private coordinate
+\[
+ \ell(\theta)\in E_n(\theta)\setminus
+ \bigcup_{\eta\in\Theta(m),\ \eta\ne\theta}T_n(\eta).
+\]
+The chosen coordinates are distinct, since a coordinate chosen for two atoms
+would lie in the full support of each and hence would not be private to either.
+There are $k$ atoms and $k$ coordinates, so $\theta\mapsto\ell(\theta)$ is a
+bijection. If $q\ne\ell(\theta)$, then $q$ is private to another atom and
+therefore cannot lie in $T_n(\theta)$. Hence
+\[
+ T_n(\theta)=E_n(\theta)=\{\ell(\theta)\}.
+\]
+Thus the inverse of \eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-bijection} sends $m$
+to its uniquely labelled atoms in the families $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$.
+
+Conversely, choose $\theta_\ell\in\mathcal A_\ell(n)$ for every
+$\ell\in\mathcal P(n)$.
+These atoms are pairwise coprime. Indeed, if
+$\theta_\ell=p^e$ and $\theta_q=p^f$ had the same underlying prime, then
+$e\ne f$ because the same atom cannot lie in two differently labelled
+families. Say $e<f$. Then $p^e\mid p^{f-1}$ would give
+\[
+ d(\theta_\ell)\mid d^-(\theta_q).
+\]
+Since $\ell$ occurs to its full $n$-adic exponent in $d(\theta_\ell)$, it
+would also occur fully in $d(\theta_q)$, contrary to
+$T_n(\theta_q)=\{q\}$ and $q\ne\ell$. The singleton full supports cover
+$\mathcal P(n)$, and the singleton essential supports are private. Hence the
+chosen atoms form an $n$-witness cover. The witness-cover theorem proves that
+their product belongs to $\mathcal M_n$ and has $k$ distinct prime factors.
+Uniqueness follows from unique factorization. This proves the bijection and
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count}.
+
+We next decide when the factors on the right of
+\eqref{eq:extremal-support-product-count} are nonzero. If $\ell$ is odd, or
+if $\ell=2$ and $a_2\ge2$, then the exact-rank existence theorem supplies a
+prime of rank $\ell^{a_\ell}$; this is an element of
+$\mathcal A_\ell(n)$. Suppose now that $a_2=1$. If $n$ is squarefree and
+$\theta\in\mathcal A_2(n)$, then $d(\theta)\mid n$ cannot contain an odd
+coordinate: every such coordinate would occur fully and would belong to
+$T_n(\theta)$. Thus $d(\theta)=2$, which is impossible because $F_2=1$ and
+$\Atom(2)=\varnothing$. Therefore the extremal slice is empty when $n$ is
+even and squarefree.
+
+If instead $a_2=1$ and $q^2\mid n$ for some odd prime $q$, take an atom of
+rank $2q$. For $q=3$, the atom $4\in\Atom(6)$ has, relative to $n$,
+$E_n(4)=T_n(4)=\{2\}$. For $q\ge5$, the rank $2q$ is nonexceptional, so an
+exact-rank prime exists and again has essential and full support $\{2\}$,
+because the $q$-coordinate is sub-full in $n$. Thus
+$\mathcal A_2(n)\ne\varnothing$. All other diagonal families were already
+seen to be nonempty, proving that the support value $k$ occurs exactly in the
+second case of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+It remains to realize every smaller support size. Assume $k\ge2$ and
+$1\le r\le k-1$. Choose a partition $\Pi$ of $\mathcal P(n)$ into $r$
+nonempty blocks, with the additional condition that $\{2\}$ is not a block
+when $a_2=1$. Such a partition exists because $r<k$. For $C\in\Pi$, put
+$n_C=\prod_{\ell\in C}\ell^{a_\ell}$ and choose
+$\theta_C\in\Atom(n_C)$. This is possible by exact-rank prime existence
+unless $n_C\in\{6,12\}$; in those two cases use respectively
+$4\in\Atom(6)$ and $16\in\Atom(12)$. The forbidden rank $2$ was excluded by
+the choice of $\Pi$. Strong divisibility makes the atoms belonging to
+disjoint blocks pairwise coprime. Their full supports are the blocks $C$, and
+each has a nonempty essential support because lowering it decreases its rank.
+They therefore form an $n$-witness cover. Its product has exactly $r$ prime
+factors, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+
+The same idea gives all connected support sizes below $k$. Choose a hub
+$h\in\mathcal P(n)$, taking $h=3$ whenever
+$\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathcal P(n)$ and $n_{\{2,3\}}\in\{6,12\}$, and partition
+$\mathcal P(n)\setminus\{h\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets $P_1,\ldots,P_r$.
+Use one atom of exact rank $n_{\{h\}\cup P_i}$ for each $i$. The only
+exceptional support that can occur is $\{2,3\}$; use $4$ at rank $6$ or $16$
+at rank $12$. In both cases its essential support contains the private
+coordinate $2\in P_i$. Every nonexceptional atom is a prime atom and has any
+coordinate of the nonempty set $P_i$ as a private coordinate. The atoms are
+pairwise coprime: their ranks are distinct, and the exceptional atom has
+underlying prime $2$, whose rank $3$ is not one of the other multi-coordinate
+ranks. The resulting witness cover is connected because all its rank-support
+edges contain $h$. Thus
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}
+ \{1,\ldots,k-1\}\subseteq\Sigma^{\rm conn}(n)\qquad(k\ge2).
+\end{equation}
+
+We finally decide whether the endpoint $k$ can be connected. In an extremal
+witness cover, write $\theta_\ell$ for the atom with
+$T_n(\theta_\ell)=\{\ell\}$ and let
+$S_\ell=\operatorname{supp}_n(d(\theta_\ell))$ be its positive-coordinate
+rank support. If $q\in S_\ell\setminus\{\ell\}$, then
+\[
+ 1\le\nu_q(d(\theta_\ell))<a_q,
+\]
+so necessarily $a_q\ge2$. If $n$ is squarefree, every $S_\ell$ is therefore
+the singleton $\{\ell\}$, and the rank-support hypergraph is disconnected
+when $k\ge2$.
+
+There is one further obstruction. Let $n=12s$ with $s$ squarefree and
+$\gcd(s,6)=1$. The only coordinate of exponent at least two is $2$. Hence an
+edge $S_3$ larger than $\{3\}$ would force $d(\theta_3)=6$. But
+$\Atom(6)=\{4\}$, and lowering $4$ gives rank $3$; relative to this $n$, the
+$3$-coordinate is not lost. Thus an atom of rank $6$ with
+$T_n(\theta_3)=\{3\}$ has empty essential support and cannot occur in a
+witness cover. Consequently $S_3=\{3\}$. Since $a_3=1$, the coordinate $3$
+cannot occur sub-fully in any other $S_\ell$, so it is isolated and the
+extremal generator is disconnected.
+
+Conversely, suppose that $n$ is nonsquarefree and is not of the preceding
+form. Choose a coordinate $h$ with $a_h\ge2$. If possible take $h\ne2$. For
+each $\ell\ne h$, choose an atom of rank
+\[
+ d_\ell=\ell^{a_\ell}h,
+\]
+and choose an exact-rank prime of rank $h^{a_h}$ for the $h$-atom. The ranks
+$d_\ell$ are nonexceptional except possibly when $h=3$ and $\ell=2$; use
+$4$ when $d_2=6$ and $16$ when $d_2=12$. These exceptional atoms have
+$E_n=T_n=\{2\}$ because the $3$-coordinate is sub-full. If the only possible
+hub is $h=2$, then either $3\nmid n$ or $a_2\ge3$. In the latter case, use
+$9\in\Atom(12)$ for the $3$-atom; relative to $n$ it has
+$E_n(9)=T_n(9)=\{3\}$. Use exact-rank primes of rank
+$\ell^{a_\ell}2$ for the remaining nonhub coordinates. In every case we have
+chosen one atom from each $\mathcal A_\ell(n)$, so the extremal-slice
+bijection makes their product a minimal generator. Its rank-support edges are
+$\{h\}$ and the pairs $\{h,\ell\}$, hence it is connected. Together with
+\eqref{eq:connected-spectrum-lower-interval}, this proves
+\eqref{eq:exact-connected-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{corollary}\label{cor:support-bound-sharp}
+For $n\ge3$, there exists $m\in\mathcal M_n$ with
+$\omega(m)=\omega(n)$ if and only if $n$ is not even and squarefree. In
+particular, equality occurs on every odd layer.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+This is the endpoint assertion in \eqref{eq:exact-total-support-spectrum}.
+\end{proof}

+## Deep Exploration Check: Exact Support Spectra
+
+Checked 2026-08-08. Fresh queries were sent to the arXiv Atom API, Crossref,
+Semantic Scholar, and zbMATH Open for Fibonacci ranks of apparition, minimal
+generators, minimal covers, connected hypergraphs, split graphs, primitive
+divisors, and strong divisibility sequences. Semantic Scholar's keyword-search
+endpoint returned HTTP 429 from the shared address, so the three nearest known
+papers were checked there by DOI instead. The API identified Hearne--Wagner,
+*Minimal Covers of Finite Sets* (1973), Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier, *Existence of
+Primitive Divisors of Lucas and Lehmer Numbers* (2001), and Renault, *The
+Period, Rank, and Order of the $(a,b)$-Fibonacci Sequence Mod $m$* (2013).
+
+The nearest combinatorial papers are Hearne--Wagner's enumeration of minimal
+covers, Royle's correspondence with split graphs, and the later split-graph
+asymptotics of Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka. The nearest arithmetic
+papers are Fulton--Morris and Lengyel on prime-power ranks, Bilu--Hanrot--
+Voutier on defective primitive-divisor indices, and Renault on the lcm rank
+identity for generalized Fibonacci sequences. The searches found no paper
+combining those inputs to classify the support sizes of minimal elements in a
+fixed Fibonacci apparition fiber, no extremal atomic-product formula, and no
+connected endpoint dichotomy involving the oriented defective rank $6$.
+
+Six candidates were compared on a five-point scale `(reach, novelty, value)`:
+
+- exact total/connected support spectra and the extremal slice: `(5,4,5)`;
+- exact realization criteria for covers meeting the even exceptional supports:
+  `(3,4,4)`;
+- support-refined polynomial connected-factorization identities: `(5,2,2)`;
+- transfer of the full witness-cover package to general Lucas sequences:
+  `(3,3,4)`;
+- complete connected four-coordinate kernel classification: `(2,4,4)`;
+- unconditional resolution of the rank-window sparsity alternatives:
+  `(1,5,5)`.
+
+The first candidate was selected. The third is a routine grading of the
+existing partition formula; the fourth needs a recurrence-specific atomic and
+defective-index analysis; the fifth is the manuscript's explicit high-support
+open project; and the sixth still needs arithmetic dispersion unavailable in
+the cited literature. The second remains plausible but requires a separate
+coprime slot classification for covers using ranks $2$, $6$, and $12$.
